indexDescription: Work through the figures behind a HubBuy purchase, from domestic delivery charges to a final parcel statement.
faq: Where do I estimate HubBuy international shipping?
Use the shipping estimator on hubbuy.com. Enter the destination, weight in grams, product category and outer dimensions in centimetres when available. Save the inputs with the displayed result.
Do the preset product weights describe my purchased item?
HubBuy labels its quick-estimate examples as approximate. Use them while planning, then replace them with measured figures from your own order and its intended packing.
Why does the estimate ask for dimensions as well as weight?
A route can have size limits or consider parcel volume when billing. Enter the actual outer length, width and height when you have them, and read the terms for the route you select.
What does seller-to-warehouse delivery pay for?

It covers the domestic movement from the seller to the receiving warehouse when such a charge applies. HubBuy lists the product purchase and China shipping before the later international parcel stage.
How should I budget two items from the same seller?
Read the final seller order summary to see whether domestic shipping is charged once or per item. Keep that amount on the seller order and allocate it only if you need per-item costs.
Can I assume separate sellers share one domestic charge?
Keep a separate purchase record for each seller. Even when purchases later travel abroad together, the domestic deliveries may have separate charges and separate tracking numbers.
When should I use a packed weight rather than the seller's item weight?
Use the packed figure for the international parcel estimate once available. It includes the box and packing materials, whereas a seller's product figure may refer only to the unit.
How do I convert kilograms for the HubBuy calculator?
Multiply kilograms by 1,000 to enter grams. A parcel measured at 1.35 kg is 1,350 g. Keep length, width and height in centimetres on the same worksheet.
Can I add three product lengths to obtain my parcel length?
Only if the items will actually be packed end to end. Decide on the proposed arrangement and measure its outer envelope. Leave room for protective material and confirm packed dimensions later.
How do I compare a single box with two boxes?
Request or calculate each option using the same items, destination and protection requirements. Compare the combined charge for both smaller parcels with the charge for the single larger parcel.
Why should I keep the quote currency beside the amount?
A number without its currency is ambiguous. Record the currency code at quotation and at payment, along with any conversion rate and fee shown, before comparing two totals.
How should an optional packing charge be recorded?
Write down the exact service, amount and whether it applies to an item or parcel. Check if a quoted total already includes it before adding it separately.
Is the cheapest displayed route suitable for every parcel?
Check destination coverage, size limits and acceptance of your actual contents. Compare delivery estimates and included services only among routes available for that parcel.
What if I change the packing after obtaining a quote?
Record what changed and rerun the estimate using the revised outer dimensions and weight. Keep the old result as a reference instead of presenting it as a quote for the new parcel.
Can I compare a product price converted by the spreadsheet directly with my card charge?

Start with the source amount, selected option and quantity. Compare conversion rate, charged currency and any explicitly listed fee on the payment record. The catalogue display is a browsing reference.
Where does a seller discount belong in the budget?
Record it beside the purchase to which it applies. Keep any outbound parcel discount separate, and check the conditions before subtracting a promotion from a planning estimate.
Why does the final total differ from my first estimate?
Compare destination, contents, route, weight, dimensions, currency, packing, discounts and service entries. Identify the first difference you can document before asking about the remaining balance.
What should I save if a support question concerns two parcels?
Save both outbound parcel references, their item lists and their final charge statements. Mark the line you are comparing on each record so the question stays tied to the correct parcel.
Can a warehouse item photo show the final packing dimensions?
An image of the product can help identify it, but the final dimensions refer to the sealed outer parcel. Ask for the packed measurements if the decision depends on fitting a route limit.
What if my order contains a fragile accessory and soft clothing?
Ask which protective arrangement is available and whether the accessory requires a separate inner box. Compare combined and separate packing after allowing for that space.
Which support site matches the HubBuy links on this grid?
The purchase links on this grid lead to hubbuy.com. Use that site's current estimator, service information and customer support for a HubBuy quote or order-specific question.

articles.title: HubBuy domestic shipping: where a seller's charge belongs in your budget
articles.lead: A delivery line can disappear from your budget or appear twice, depending on where you write it. Follow one seller order to the warehouse before assigning any part of that charge to an international parcel.
sections: Follow the physical delivery

HubBuy's public purchase guide describes paying for the product and shipping within China at the ordering stage. International shipping appears later, after warehousing and the selection of items to send abroad. Draw the journey on a scrap of paper. Put the shop on the left, the receiving warehouse in the middle and your address on the right. Mark which leg the delivery charge on your screen actually covers. A seller's promise of free delivery may answer the first question while leaving the last leg entirely open.
Read one order before dividing the charge

Suppose one shop supplies two T-shirts at 68 yuan each and a cap at 42 yuan. The checkout shows a single domestic charge of 10 yuan. The seller order totals 188 yuan. Three separate rows in your shortlist should not turn that into three charges of 10. Keep the 10 on a summary line until you have a reason to calculate the cost of an individual piece. Record who collected the payment and which seller order number appears beside it.
Choose an allocation method suited to your question

If two people share the order, agreeing on a split matters more than producing a falsely precise cost per item. A simple split across three units gives approximately 3.33 yuan per piece with a one-cent rounding adjustment. Another method assigns the 10 in proportion to product value. Each 68-yuan shirt gets about 3.82 and the cap about 2.36. Both methods reproduce 188. Neither method can establish the seller's actual transport cost for the cap.
When one seller sends two boxes

A second domestic tracking number can appear if the shop sends items separately. Look for a new payment line before adding a second shipping cost. One seller order can have two deliveries, just as one delivery can contain multiple garments. Track the boxes separately for receipt but keep the financial record tied to what was actually charged. If an item has not arrived, a delivery scan for the first box tells you very little about the location of the second.
What changes after a cancellation

If the cap is cancelled, avoid immediately subtracting 42 from the old total and treating the result as settled. Check the refund statement for the product amount and any domestic adjustment. The original allocation may now describe goods that never travelled together. Keep the original order and add a dated credit row, then calculate the remaining cost from the surviving items. Ask for clarification with the purchase reference if the domestic charge has no corresponding adjustment explanation.
A worked comparison with two sellers

Consider a buyer choosing between two offers for the same packs of plain socks. Shop Green lists the selected packs at 24 yuan each and shows 8 yuan domestic delivery for the order. Shop Blue lists them at 26 each with domestic delivery included in the displayed checkout. At a quantity of one, Green costs 32 and Blue costs 26. At a quantity of three, the totals are 80 and 78. At a quantity of four, both cost 104. These break-even figures assume the prices and delivery conditions remain fixed as quantity changes. Open each checkout again at the intended quantity before basing a purchase on the calculation.

Now imagine that the seller applies a five-pack price tier. That changes the comparison because one of the inputs has moved. A spreadsheet formula that extrapolated the four-pack comparison would miss it. Write the observed totals for one, three, four and five packs as separate scenarios, with the exact option used in each. Keep the marketplace address beside each result. A shop's price for a short pack of socks is no evidence about the price of a longer pack, even when the picture shows the same colour assortment.
Splitting the cost of a group order

Two friends agree to buy from one shop. Mei chooses one garment costing 120 yuan and Arun chooses four accessories at 20 yuan each. The single domestic charge is 12. Dividing by five units gives Mei 2.40 and Arun 9.60 of the delivery cost. Dividing in proportion to merchandise value gives Mei 7.20 and Arun 4.80. Splitting the delivery equally makes each share six. All three methods reconcile to the same total. The important question is which agreement the people sharing the bill intend, not which method produces the lowest price for a particular person's line.

Put that agreement in the note accompanying the order before asking either friend to settle. Record the original 12 as the amount on the seller order. Then display the chosen allocation in a separate column. If you later need to ask HubBuy about the domestic charge, send the seller-order figure. Sending one friend's allocated share as if it were the amount charged would create a discrepancy that exists only in your own accounting.
Separating a seller's refund from a delivery refund

Consider a seller that receives payment for two 65-yuan pieces and one 12-yuan domestic charge. One piece cannot be supplied. The transaction history then shows a confirmed refund of 65. The net payment is 77. That total is consistent with one remaining piece and the original delivery charge, but it does not tell you whether a revised shipping arrangement was discussed. Check the refund description and the terms for the seller order before attributing a reason to it.

If a second credit of 6 appears later, record it on the date it posts and retain its reference. Your final net becomes 71. Do not retroactively change the original 12 to 6 and also include the six-unit credit; that would reduce your ledger twice. In a group order, decide whether a changed charge requires a revised split. The person who cancelled may still have agreed to share domestic delivery. That is a settlement choice among buyers and separate from the seller's accounting.
Reading common pieces of evidence

A listing screenshot is useful for identifying the offer and the date. It may show a shipping statement for a default address, a default option or a promotional threshold that your order does not meet. A checkout screenshot with the exact options and receiving destination provides a better estimate. A payment confirmation tied to the seller order establishes what was actually collected. A refund record establishes a later movement. Preserve this sequence rather than replacing every earlier document with the latest one.

Warehousing evidence answers a different question. A courier label can identify which package travelled. A warehouse entry can identify the items recorded as received. Neither document independently tells you how the seller calculated the price. If you need to connect a missing piece to a cost question, include the order summary and the delivery references together. For example, state that order X showed one domestic charge and two packages were received, and ask whether a second charge shown elsewhere belongs to this seller. Give support an identifiable line to investigate.
A quick check before accepting the total

Read your worksheet from left to right. Can you point to the selected selling unit, the number purchased, the seller-level subtotal, the domestic charge collected, any later credit and the resulting net? Mark any estimate that still rests on an unconfirmed delivery price. If the merchandise is already paid for and a friend only needs an approximate per-item share, explain the allocation method and its rounding. If you are comparing two live sellers, use their full domestic totals at the same quantity. Save international shipping for the parcel comparison, where its own inputs can be checked.

articles.title: How to read a HubBuy service or packing charge on a quote
articles.lead: Before comparing the size of two charges, identify what each service does, which object it applies to and whether it has already entered the amount due.
sections: Give each charge a unit

HubBuy links separately to Service & Fees and Logistics Shipping Fees. Open the current description that matches the stage you are reviewing. Copy the name as it appears on your statement. Write a unit beside it: one purchased unit, one order, one packed box or one international parcel. A figure of six beside a packing option means something different if it is applied once per parcel than if it is applied to each item.
Work through a quotation with mixed units

Consider a hypothetical worksheet with three product entries, two inner cartons and one outer parcel. Assume the quoted service is 4 yuan per inner carton and an outer-packing option costs 7 yuan for the parcel. The worksheet should add 8 and 7, or 15 in total. Multiplying both charges by three because there are three item rows produces 33. This example illustrates the arithmetic only; read the actual service units and amounts on the live offer.
Separate optional and included services

Read the quote in the state in which you intend to purchase it. A checkbox with a price beside it describes a possible selection. A selected checkbox and corresponding subtotal tell you more. Record the initial base, activate the desired service and compare the new amount, currency and named lines. Keep a note if the price display already bundles the service. Adding the visible price again outside the quote would inflate the apparent cost.
Keep evidence of the requested work

A service name alone may be ambiguous after dispatch. If you need a bag protected from crushing, write down whether you asked for an inner box, corner protection or to keep the original packaging. Retain the confirmation attached to the parcel. If the result differs, show what was requested and which visible feature is missing. Support can investigate a specific operation more readily than a general complaint about expensive packing.
Read an adjustment without erasing the original quote

Use separate rows for quoted, paid and credited amounts. If a charge was removed, enter the credit with its reference. When a final invoice rolls services into a parcel subtotal, place that subtotal in a comparison column rather than adding it to the detailed entries. Check that your reconstructed total agrees with the payment record within ordinary rounding. Write down the remaining difference and ask support which invoice line explains it.
Reconstructing a service total from a receipt

Here is a fictional receipt to practise with. Two fragile pieces require individual protective wrapping at 3 yuan per piece. One outer box uses a 9-yuan reinforcement option. The quoted base freight is 118. A screen then shows a parcel total of 133. The numbers reconcile because 118 plus six plus nine is 133. The words per piece and per parcel make the arithmetic reproducible. Without them, two buyers could look at the same three numbers and arrive at different totals.

Suppose the final invoice shows 124 as freight including the two protective wraps and 9 on a separate line. The total is still 133. It would be misleading to report a new six-yuan increase merely because the value called freight rose from 118 to 124. Compare the composition of each displayed figure before comparing its magnitude. If the final description does not make clear whether the wraps are inside the 124, ask for the breakdown. Record an unresolved question instead of changing a line description to make the numbers fit.
What to do when the same service appears twice

A familiar label can denote two legitimate operations. An item-level service can prepare one fragile object before it enters a parcel, while a parcel-level service can reinforce the outer box. Open the details of each entry and compare the object being handled, the quantity and the stated purpose. If one charge is attached to a purchase reference and another to an outbound parcel, save both references. A shared word such as protection does not establish a duplicate.

Conversely, a service can appear in a list of selected options and again in a payment summary because the summary repeats its components. Compare the amount due with and without the charge included once. If including it once already reproduces the payment, the second display is probably a different view of the same amount. State what your arithmetic demonstrates and leave the internal accounting explanation to the provider. The goal is to identify a real mismatch, not to infer a duplicate from typography.
Ask for an outcome you can identify

The service description should tell you what will be done to the object. A request to protect a bag could mean filling its interior to retain shape, keeping its original box or placing it in a larger outer carton. Each choice may affect the parcel differently. Specify the object, the result you need and any condition such as keeping detachable handles together. Then read what the selected service actually promises. If it covers only an outer carton, do not count it as individual protection for every item inside.

If the request changes, keep the first quotation and add the new one. Record which service was removed and whether its replacement has a different unit. Consider replacing one outer-box option costing ten with individual protection costing four for each of three units. The new selected services total twelve, a difference of two. Adding twelve to the old ten would describe buying both alternatives, which was never the instruction. A dated note beside each version helps later if the two appear in separate account messages.
Distinguish a cost comparison from a quality judgment

A lower service price is useful only if it addresses the actual concern. Someone sending replacement parts may care that small components stay bundled. Someone sending a gift might care that the retail carton remains intact. These people can receive identical freight quotes yet make different rational decisions about optional work. Write a one-sentence acceptance condition for each service you consider. For a loose accessory, it could be that it remains with its known parent item inside the package.

After delivery, compare that condition with what you can observe. A well-protected outer corner is not evidence that an internal accessory was separately wrapped. If an instruction appears to have been missed, show the order acknowledgement, the selected service and a picture of the relevant part of the received package. Avoid attributing damage to a particular event without evidence. State the requested outcome and what you found, then ask which next step applies.
A support message that isolates an unexplained amount

Begin with the parcel reference, currency and exact service label. State the amount you can reconcile and the remaining difference. For instance: my summary shows two wraps at three each and a carton at nine, totalling fifteen; my service subtotal is eighteen; please identify the remaining three. Add the relevant quote date and a cropped image of the service lines if necessary. Exclude unrelated orders and personal payment details. One concrete arithmetic question gives support a practical starting point.

When a reply comes back, enter the provider's explanation beside the line it concerns. If the difference is a previously unseen quantity, correct the quantity column. If it is an already established charge, link it to the earlier entry rather than creating another. Once the detailed services, freight and credits reproduce the statement, your worksheet can serve two purposes: checking the present transaction and building a more realistic estimate for a future parcel with similar requirements.

articles.title: Pricing a HubBuy order with several options from the same seller
articles.lead: Multiple choices on one marketplace listing can mean different units, quantities and prices. Build the estimate from confirmed options before applying delivery or discounts.
sections: Make the seller's selling unit explicit

Read each option before copying the lowest displayed price. A listing can offer a complete set, a single piece, a replacement part or more than one pack size. Save the seller's option text in its original language as well as your translation. If you are buying two shirts in one colour and another in a different size, give them separate lines. An entry saying only three shirts gives you no way to check which line changed when the seller confirms part of the order.
Build the merchandise subtotal first

For example, assume the selected medium shirt costs 72 yuan, the large costs 76 and the two-piece set costs 130. Selecting two medium shirts and one set costs 274 before delivery. Accidentally using the 72-yuan shirt price for the set gives 216. The 58-yuan difference comes from selecting the wrong unit, not from a hidden freight charge. Keeping pack type, option, unit price and quantity in separate columns makes the error visible.
Check minimums and tiers against the selected mix

A seller may display several quantity tiers. Read whether quantities can be mixed across colours and whether the minimum is per style or total. For a hypothetical offer priced at 55 per piece for four or more, a basket of three may still use the lower-volume price. Count complete selling units. Two pairs in a two-pair pack can be one selling unit even though the warehouse receives four individual articles.
Split a discount using the rule printed on the order

Look at the seller summary before allocating the saving. A promotion may apply only to certain items or may change when a unit is cancelled. Keep the eligibility conditions with the order. When you simply need to share a bill, state your allocation method separately from the seller's calculation. For example, proportional distribution among eligible items may be fair among friends but does not describe which refund the seller will approve later.
Carry item identities into the warehouse

Give each line a stable name, such as navy shirt medium or blue set large. When two deliveries appear, match warehouse entries to those names and counts. Keep one cancelled line in the ledger as cancelled rather than reusing its identifier for another piece. Before submitting a parcel, compare the count of completed entries against what you paid for. A total that balances financially can still conceal a missing colour or an incomplete set.
Buying for three people from one option grid

Imagine three friends choosing trousers from one listing. One selects the unlined version in size medium, another selects the lined version in medium and the third selects the unlined version in large. The listing title and seller number are identical on all three records. The information that distinguishes them lives in the option columns. Write one complete selection per line and name the recipient in your private sheet. If the seller option names are translated alike, keep the original wording and thumbnail beside the selections.

Suppose the confirmed unit prices are 80, 94 and 80 yuan and the order has one 9-yuan domestic charge. The merchandise total is 254 and the order total is 263. If the payment request shows 269, inspect its components before calling the extra six a service charge. The seller may have changed the price of one variant, added an explicit charge or applied a different quantity. Compare each option, quantity and line subtotal in order. A three-line purchase is small enough to reconcile without guessing which part changed.
Checking a multi-pack against single units

A second shop offers a pair of plain socks individually or as a five-pair pack. Four single pairs at 12 each cost 48. A five-pair pack at 55 costs 11 per pair, yet requires a larger outlay and leaves an extra pair. The cheaper per-pair price does not automatically answer which option suits a buyer who needs exactly four. Compare both the total cash required and the number of useful units that will actually be used.

Read the size and colour assortment on the pack. A five-pack may contain an assortment chosen by the seller rather than five duplicates of a selected colour. If only two pairs match the need, dividing by five is a misleading measure of value to that buyer. Before paying, write a sentence describing exactly what should arrive: five wearable pairs in size X, with the colours distributed as stated in option Y. This sentence becomes a usable warehouse count instead of a number with no physical meaning.
Handling a partial stock confirmation

Take the example of two medium shirts and a set. If the seller confirms only one medium shirt, the original 274 no longer describes the goods available. One shirt at 72 plus the set at 130 gives a merchandise total of 202. Check whether a quantity threshold, domestic delivery condition or discount has changed as well. A cancellation can affect more than the removed unit if the promotion depended on the original basket.

Keep the old quote and add a revised quote under it. If the larger amount was already paid, track the credit process separately from the recalculated cost. Do not enter 202 as the only payment when the account shows 274 collected and a credit still pending. The two records answer different questions: what the retained merchandise should cost, and which funds have actually moved. Keep the same line names so that a friend reviewing the change can tell which item became unavailable.
Identifying a quantity mistake before it travels

A photograph of three unopened packets can confirm that three packets are present. It may not confirm the number of units inside each. For a set with different contents per package, ask for a view or label that distinguishes the package versions without damaging packaging the seller may require. For separate garment sizes, match each readable size tag to a line on the paid order, especially when two colours differ only slightly under warehouse lighting.

If you receive one packet with a handwritten count of four, compare that with the seller's stated packing unit before reporting a shortage. Four accessories inside one bag may fulfill four units, whereas four empty protective sleeves do not. Describe the observable fact in your message and ask a concrete question. For instance, the order includes three two-piece sets and the warehouse entry shows three sealed packages; could you verify whether each package contains both listed pieces?
Keeping product mathematics separate from outbound freight

The price per usable item can be useful before purchase, but do not silently add a future international fee to each seller line and treat the result as confirmed. Once the goods arrive, a shared parcel may contain items from several purchases and use packing that was unknown earlier. Retain the confirmed seller costs and add a separate outbound comparison when measured figures become available. If you later allocate freight among recipients, document that policy separately.

A complete record lets you answer three questions without recalculating from memory. Which version and quantity did the seller agree to supply? How much was actually collected or returned on the purchase? Which items are ready for international submission? A purchase line can be financially complete while one piece is still waiting for identification, so close each line only when its contents and its payment history are both clear.

articles.title: Budgeting a HubBuy basket supplied by different sellers
articles.lead: A multi-shop shortlist can look like one cart, while costs and delivery events still originate with different sellers. Organize the purchase by shop first and the international shipment by parcel later.
sections: Create a small register for each seller

Save the original listing, chosen option, quantity, product amount and domestic delivery shown for that particular purchase. Put discounts under the shop where they apply. Two listings sharing the same studio photo can still be offered by different sellers. Use the shop identity and the marketplace listing number to distinguish them, and give the lines names you will recognize even if the seller edits the title.
Keep committed costs separate from intentions

Suppose shop A has confirmed a 90-yuan jacket and 8 yuan delivery. Shop B still shows a 54-yuan scarf with domestic delivery unknown. Shop C has cancelled a 30-yuan accessory and its refund has not arrived. Show 98 as the confirmed purchase cost for A, 54 plus an unresolved amount as the estimate for B and 30 as a pending credit if it was actually paid. Adding everything into one definite subtotal would hide three different states.
Track arrivals without changing the accounting basis

The parcel that reaches the warehouse first may belong to the last shop you ordered from. An arrival changes what you can inspect or submit for shipping, but does not automatically create an additional seller charge. Record the domestic tracking reference against the purchase and the warehouse reference against the received unit. If two tracking numbers arrive for one seller order, confirm the contents of each before treating either shipment as complete.
Decide what waiting for the last item costs

Write down the warehouse deadlines for the items already stored and the latest confirmed information for the missing piece. Compare a combined parcel when all items arrive with sending the ready items now. Do not assign an invented cost to waiting. If a storage charge or packing service could matter, check the current account information. If the item has a firm use date, represent that constraint separately from the freight comparison.
Rebuild the final total from its records

Start with net merchandise across sellers. Add the domestic amounts actually charged once each, then add outbound parcel payments and any separately shown services. Subtract refunds only when you can match them to the correct purchase, currency and destination. A refund returned to an account balance may affect your usable balance differently from a credit to your original payment method. Keep both the economic cost and the payment history visible.
A basket that changes while the first item is in storage

Imagine you have chosen a coat from one shop, a scarf from another and two bags from a third. The coat is received first. The scarf seller confirms the original colour is unavailable, and the bag seller sends two domestic tracking numbers. On your sheet you now have one ready item, one unresolved purchase and two shipments linked to one purchase. Listing all four items as ready would result in a parcel plan the warehouse cannot yet fulfill.

Work out two possible shopping baskets. In the first, the scarf is cancelled and the coat and both bags are retained. In the second, you accept a different scarf and wait for its arrival. Show confirmed costs shared by both scenarios once and note the costs and risks that differ. The first option may change freight by removing an item; the second may change warehouse timing. Neither estimate is complete until you have the measurements and services for the parcel you actually intend to submit.
Deciding who owes what in a shared basket

Suppose one friend buys from shop A only and another friend buys from shops B and C. Individual seller charges belong to the appropriate purchase first. The friends might then agree to divide the international shipping equally, by weight or according to another rule. Keep that private agreement separate from the charges the sellers or HubBuy applied. A buyer's contribution can change when the packing plan changes even if no seller has altered its own amount.

For example, three purchases might have net totals of 106, 64 and 180 yuan. Their combined purchase cost is 350. If one purchase later gets a 20-yuan credit, the new cost is 330. Assign that credit to the purchase it belongs to before splitting anything else. Subtracting it from the international parcel total would make it harder to explain either the net seller cost or the eventual outbound charge. Show a pending credit separately until it actually appears.
Inventory matching across deliveries

Use a unique row identifier for each chosen option. A short name such as coat-A-small is enough in a personal worksheet if it also points to the underlying order reference. When an intake notification arrives, match the item to a row using the seller, domestic tracking and identifying details. If two similar bags came from different shops, a studio picture shared by both shops is weaker evidence than the corresponding delivery record.

If a delivery appears without an obvious match, do not immediately reassign it to whichever row is still blank. Check how many pieces each seller was expected to send, the last known tracking events and any note about a split delivery. Contact support with the specific unresolved record and the candidate orders. A clear inquiry might say that two domestic numbers were expected from shop C, one has an identifiable bag in stock, and you need help matching the second number to its intake.
Planning the outbound comparison with unresolved costs

Keep unknown amounts visibly unknown. A blank field frequently gets treated as zero when a spreadsheet sums a column. Add a status such as awaiting domestic quote to flag a missing charge. If the seller confirms a range instead of a final amount, preserve both endpoints for planning and mark the calculation as conditional. Use the exact amount on the confirmed payment record when it becomes available.

You can still make a useful decision with one missing number. Assume the confirmed items total 250 yuan and the preferred basket has a hard merchandise budget of 300. There is 50 left for the unresolved item plus any remaining seller charges. If the item's selected price alone exceeds 50, you already know this plan will exceed that budget, even before international freight. If the selected item costs 40, the decision turns on the remaining conditions. The calculation identifies what you need to ask next.
Closing the basket without losing its history

After delivery, keep a final list of which purchases ended up in which parcel. Some may be returned, sent later or accepted as replacements. If you sent the coat earlier and the two bags later, the original one-box estimate is useful historical information, not the final transport bill. Enter two outbound references and their confirmed amounts. Where an amount is in another currency, retain its original value and the actual converted payment entry.

Finish by checking arithmetic in stages. Sum retained merchandise by shop. Add domestic delivery shown on the relevant purchases. Apply confirmed seller credits. Add final parcel payments and separately billed services only once. Reconcile any friend-to-friend allocation to the result. The resulting total can then be traced to records the people involved can inspect, including the reason the final basket differs from the first shortlist.

articles.title: Comparing HubBuy quotes when the currencies differ
articles.lead: Two screenshots can show different numbers for the same purchase without showing a different underlying price. Work from a common currency, a stated conversion direction and an identical set of included charges.
sections: Decide what you are comparing

A catalogue conversion helps with browsing. A merchant quotation shows an amount offered in a particular currency. A card statement shows what was actually posted. Write which of those three you have beside every number. Do not replace the source currency when you translate a quote into your home currency. Keep the original information available so you can recalculate later without relying on a rounded display.
Make the exchange-rate direction readable

Imagine a teaching example in which one home-currency unit buys 7.20 yuan. A 360-yuan quote corresponds to 50 units before fees because 360 is divided by 7.20. If you instead record the rate as home units per yuan, multiply by that number. Write out both currency codes with the rate. A single bare value such as 7.20 is especially easy to use backwards when a sheet mixes several quotations.
Normalize inclusions before the rate

Suppose quote A covers the same merchandise and domestic delivery as quote B, but only A includes protective packing. Compare the contents before worrying about exchange-rate rounding. Either add the confirmed packing amount to B or label the quotes as different offers. If a missing charge has no confirmed amount, leave a gap instead of filling it with an attractive guess. A conversion cannot repair two quotes that describe different services.
Include payment fees exactly once

A card might show one all-in home-currency debit, or separate conversion and service entries. Record what the statement actually shows. If the statement amount is already converted and includes a fee, treating that total as a new source amount and applying another conversion repeats the adjustment. When comparing a live quote with a posted charge, document the quote time and posting date. A later rate can differ even when the merchandise price is identical.
Round at the point where payment rounds

When a seller summary collects several lines into one payment, convert the original-currency subtotal for your comparison. Rounding every small item first can create a few cents of difference from converting the order once. For a reimbursement sheet you may still need per-person figures. State which line absorbs the rounding remainder so that the sum of the allocations matches the amount actually paid.
Worked example with a fixed fee

Take a fictional payment in which the base amount is 300 yuan and the comparison rate is 7.50 yuan per home-currency unit. The base conversion gives 40.00. One hypothetical payment method adds a fixed fee of 1.30 home units. Another has no fixed fee but quotes a conversion that results in 41.00. For this amount, the second method would cost 0.30 less, provided both figures are final and cover the same goods and services. The lower quoted exchange figure alone does not determine the result.

Now change the purchase to 75 yuan using the same illustrative conditions. The first method gives 10.00 plus 1.30, while an equally sized percentage difference on the second method might have a very different effect in absolute terms. Recalculate instead of assuming the method that won on the first purchase also wins here. Fixed fees matter proportionally more on small payments. These invented numbers explain comparison mechanics only and make no claim about the methods, rates or fees offered to any HubBuy account.
Keep a consistent direction in a mixed-currency worksheet

If one seller quotes in yuan and another amount already appears in your home currency, define a single comparison column. Convert each source amount into that column once. A simple note next to the source amount should give its unit and the conversion direction. Enter 150 CNY and 7.50 CNY per home unit as separate fields. Check that the converted result times 7.50 returns the source amount before any fees.

A common mistake occurs when a friend pastes a displayed conversion into a column that ordinarily contains original yuan amounts. The sheet then converts an amount that has already been converted, creating an implausibly low total. Use clear column names and keep screenshots or payment references close to the corresponding row. If you cannot tell which currency a pasted number uses, leave it out of the combined total until you can identify its unit.
Compare estimates at the same point in the transaction

A product card viewed in the morning and a payment statement issued days later are different observations. Changes in selected variant, quantity, discounts or payment method can alter the result before exchange rates are considered. Begin by reconstructing the original-currency merchandise subtotal. Add domestic shipping and any services the relevant screen includes. Only once both source subtotals describe the same purchase should you compare conversion rates.

For a parcel, keep packed measurements and route consistent as well. If the first screenshot was a quick estimate for one jacket and the second a final all-in payment for a larger consolidated package, no exchange-rate calculation can make them a fair pair. Mark the physical change first. If useful, obtain a new estimate for the same parcel inputs in the current display currency and state its date. An old figure can explain the history even when it cannot answer the present comparison.
What a refund can and cannot tell you

A refund statement may show the original currency even when your card posts a home-currency credit. Record the two values in their own columns, matched by reference where possible. A different home-currency credit from the original debit can reflect several factors. Check the amount refunded in the original currency, the payment destination, any stated fee and the dates of the transactions before attributing a difference to exchange.

Suppose a 150-yuan line was originally included within a larger payment. The later credit may refer to that one line only, not a proportion of every service on the initial order. Domestic delivery or optional work may have separate terms. Use the explicit refund breakdown or ask about the named purchase. Applying an old per-item estimate that included an allocated share of freight can create a supposed shortfall that the actual refund statement never promised to cover.
Use a range when today's decision precedes payment

Sometimes a buyer needs a planning figure before the exact transaction rate is known. Show a sensitivity range using clearly labelled hypothetical rates instead of presenting a single amount as guaranteed. For a 450-yuan amount, 7.50 yuan per home unit produces 60.00, while 7.20 produces 62.50, before any additional charges. That 2.50 spread identifies how much the assumption matters for this hypothetical budget. It does not predict the rate available at checkout.

When you receive the actual payment record, preserve your range and add the posted result beside it. State which differences came from the observed conversion and which came from changed contents or services. Share the source currency, the conversion used and the total amount due together whenever you discuss the quote with another person. This way the comparison can be reproduced without relying on a symbol such as a dollar sign that might refer to several different currencies.
A practical final check

Before accepting a number from a screenshot, identify the currency code and whether the price covers one unit, the selected quantity or the entire parcel. Save any quoted conversion alongside the original amount. Someone reviewing the purchase later should be able to reproduce the converted value using those saved inputs, even after the currency selector displays a different rate.

articles.title: HubBuy packing choices: comparing protection and base freight
articles.lead: A service can change the parcel twice: once through its own price and again through its effect on the finished box. Capture those effects separately before choosing how to pack.
sections: Start with what needs protection

Decide which part of the purchase must arrive in a particular condition. The concern might be a thin handle, vulnerable corners or a retail box needed as a gift. A request for the cheapest packing leaves the warehouse guessing about your priorities. Identify the item and the feature that matters. If keeping a retail box affects your decision, ask before authorizing its removal, particularly while any exchange question remains open.
Define comparable packing options

In a teaching example, option A uses an existing carton and simple padding. Option B adds an inner protective shell. Write the cost of each quoted service, then measure or request the external weight and dimensions of the finished parcel under each arrangement. The shell may change the size available to a route, even if it adds little weight. Enter the same destination and product category for both estimates.
Separate the two price effects

Suppose a hypothetical quote rises from 150 to 166 after a service is selected. If the service itself is listed at 10 and the packing changes the freight line by 6, record both changes. If the quote shows only an all-in increase of 16, report that observed difference and leave its composition unresolved. Do not present the whole 16 as the service fee or add the visible 10 on top of the already updated total.
Look at packaging removal as a trade-off

Removing an empty spacer can reduce volume without changing the protection needed. Removing a rigid box from an item that depends on it for shape is a different decision. Identify what will replace the original protection. Ask whether parts such as cards, straps, wrapping or detachable pieces will be retained. If your concern is size rather than weight, check the finished longest side instead of assuming that discarding a box always changes the available routes.
Before accepting the packing result

Compare the warehouse's confirmed instructions with the quote, the selected content list and any submitted measurement request. If an item has been removed from the parcel, update your old comparison. Keep the record of what was requested separate from what was observed. A final packed weight is evidence of the weight; it does not reveal whether a delicate edge was padded internally.
Comparing two versions of a mixed parcel

Imagine a rigid accessory case and two soft shirts. The accessory case has a latch that should not bear pressure. In arrangement A, all three items sit in one tight carton with the shirts around the case. In arrangement B, the case has a separate padded sleeve within a larger outer box. Ask what protection each service actually supplies and whether the packed dimensions are confirmed or estimated. The second arrangement can provide different protection while also changing the available freight route.

Suppose the live representative figures you write down for an illustrative exercise are 130 for freight and 4 for the basic packing in A, compared with 136 for freight and 11 for the more protective service in B. The totals are 134 and 147. The extra cost of B is 13, consisting of six more in freight and seven more in selected packing. If the 136 already includes the protective service, the calculation changes. The wording of the line matters as much as the numbers, which are fictional and do not describe HubBuy's price list.
Decide what information is worth obtaining

Before asking a warehouse to prepare two complete alternatives, identify which uncertainty drives your decision. If keeping a retail carton is essential, comparing a box-free arrangement wastes time. If a route has a maximum outer dimension, the useful question may be whether the existing carton fits once protection is added. If the estimator shows a result for only one product category, clarify route acceptance for all contents instead of treating cheap packing as the deciding factor.

Ask about any service charge for a change or for obtaining additional measurements. Do not assume that an alternative packing arrangement can be trialled, reversed and photographed without cost. Record what the account actually offers. A sensible short message identifies the current parcel, the protection that must remain and the measurement you need. For example, a buyer could ask whether the shortest eligible box that retains the protective insert will stay below a stated route limit. A useful answer concerns that precise plan.
Recognize when cost per kilogram is the wrong measure

Some buyers compare packing by dividing the invoice by the scale weight. A heavier but better protected version may appear cheaper per kilogram even though it costs more overall. Conversely, a lighter parcel with a larger outer box may cost more on a route that considers volume. Use the total charge for the parcel that actually fulfills your requirements. Keep a per-kilogram calculation only when it helps answer a secondary comparison.

Consider a fictional box costing 150 at 2 kg and another costing 160 at 2.5 kg. Their apparent costs per kilogram are 75 and 64. The lower unit figure belongs to the more expensive parcel. It may still be the better choice if the extra protective materials serve a real need, but the numerical ratio alone cannot settle that. A buyer evaluating whether to add protection should instead look at the incremental ten, the change in dimensions and the value of preserving the required condition.
Separate removable packaging from essential components

A cloth bag inside a box might be disposable packing, a dust cover included with the merchandise or a separately paid accessory. Specify which you mean before asking for removal. Where several items carry loose parts, list the pieces that must remain together. Save the original option description if the item's completeness or potential return depends on a particular pouch or box. If the identity of a component is unclear, request clarification before allowing disposal.

A useful packing record can be short. Write one line per item stating retain, remove or ask, followed by the physical object concerned. For example, retain the protective insert around the handle, remove the empty seller dispatch carton if permitted, and ask before discarding the outer retail box. This makes the instruction understandable even when two boxes have similar dimensions. It also helps you interpret a photograph of the contents before sealing.
Compare the result with the instruction

Keep the final parcel statement next to your selected services and measured outer dimensions. If the outbound charge changes, compare the final dimensions with the size assumed earlier. If the invoice shows an additional service, identify which piece and which instruction it corresponds to. If there is no clear match, ask support to explain the line and supply the quote you were comparing.

At receipt, preserve photographs of the box and its internal arrangement if you need to report a problem. Document the visible condition; a photograph cannot establish where along the journey an impact occurred. Link the parcel reference, requested protection and observed outcome. Keep financial reconciliation and a condition complaint distinct even when both arise from the same shipment. One concerns which services were paid for, while the other concerns the condition in which the goods arrived.

articles.title: How to measure a packed parcel for the HubBuy shipping estimator
articles.lead: Three lengths and one weight are useful only if they describe the same finished box. Measure in the units the estimator expects and record how you obtained each number.
sections: Identify the parcel being measured

Write down its contents and whether retail boxes and extra protection are included. Measure the outer package that would travel, not the folded garment or its original product box alone. If you only have measurements supplied by a seller, label them accordingly. HubBuy's estimator offers approximate product presets as starting points and also accepts manual information. Use the more specific measurement when it genuinely describes your parcel.
Capture the largest outer spans

Measure length, width and height perpendicular to each other, including protruding parts of the packaging. Do not use the interior dimensions printed on an empty carton when a packed lid bulges. Place the package on a stable surface. If asking someone else to measure, request centimetres, the outside of the sealed parcel and a note identifying which box they measured. Save the figures with the parcel reference.
Keep the scale reading in the right unit

The HubBuy form asks for grams. A reading of 1.45 kilograms is 1,450 grams; a reading of 145 grams is an entirely different parcel. Include the packaging and contents on the scale together. A seller's weight for one unit multiplied by the number ordered gives only an initial idea. The finished carton, protection and any original boxes can change the final figure.
Understand what volume tells you

A hypothetical box measuring 40 by 30 by 20 centimetres has an outer rectangular volume of 24,000 cubic centimetres. A second box measuring 40 by 30 by 15 has 18,000. The reduced height removes a quarter of that geometric volume. Whether it changes freight depends on the chosen route's limits and billing rules, which must be checked on the actual offer. Avoid assigning a general dimensional divisor to every route.
Recheck after the final modification

Adding a corner protector or moving an item into another carton can change a dimension even when the overall weight scarcely moves. Keep one dated measurement record for each arrangement. A photograph showing a tape around the box's perimeter cannot establish the three separate side lengths on its own. If one figure looks implausible, ask to see the measurement from start to end before submitting numbers to the calculator.
A dimensional comparison you can reproduce

Take an example of an empty carton whose inside is labelled 35 by 25 by 15 centimetres. After loading it and applying protection, the outside measures 36 by 26 by 17. The inside rectangular volume is 13,125 cubic centimetres. The outside rectangular volume is 15,912, a difference of 2,787. This discrepancy can arise without adding a second product. The box walls, the lid and a bulging section can all matter to the outer measurement.

The two numbers answer different questions. Internal volume helps you reason about what might fit. External volume describes the space the packed box occupies. For a route comparison based on outer dimensions, keep the latter. The percentage change in geometric volume is about 21 percent, yet it would be a mistake to predict a 21 percent change in freight. The current route defines the billing method and restrictions. A volume comparison is a measurement exercise, not a complete price calculation.
Handling soft and irregular shapes

A soft parcel can change dimensions depending on how it rests. Measure the maximum outer span as it would travel, including a thick pocket of material or protective padding. If it is later enclosed in a rigid carton, use the carton dimensions instead. Avoid pressing a soft measurement flat to obtain an attractive number unless the actual packing method keeps it that way. A parcel that expands after measuring no longer corresponds to the estimate.

For an irregular object, record the length, width and height of its enclosing package rather than tracing curves around the object. A tape following the arc of a handle produces a distance along a curve. It does not show how wide the finished parcel is. Where the longest projection is hard to identify, request a wide view of the completed package and the measured spans. Label any estimate based on an unpacked object as provisional until the outer dimensions are known.
Comparing two readings from different people

A warehouse message might give 17 centimetres for height while an older seller diagram showed 14. Before asking which figure is wrong, identify what each person measured. The diagram could refer to the product, a folded product, an inner carton or the package before reinforcement. Ask for the outer parcel reference and the time of measurement. A difference can be completely reasonable when the objects measured are different.

If both records supposedly refer to the same finished parcel, compare the orientation and endpoints. A tape starting at the bottom edge of a recessed panel and ending at the centre of a flat lid may miss protected corners that project farther. Ask for the longest outside span rather than the measurement across the central panel. Keep a generous uncertainty in a planning figure when the parcel sits close to an eligibility limit. Final acceptance depends on the carrier and the route's actual rule.
Protecting the unit conversion

Create three input fields whose names include cm, then a separate weight field labelled g. If your scale reports ounces or pounds, convert before entering the number and retain the original reading beside the converted value. For a conversion from kilograms, a simple check is to divide the entered grams by 1,000 and confirm you recover your starting reading. A suspiciously tiny value should prompt a unit check before a search for cheaper routes.

Several items can arrive with individually recorded weights. Adding those figures provides a starting estimate for contents, but the sum omits the final outer packaging and may include packaging that will later be removed. If there are two outbound boxes, do not enter their total weight alongside the dimensions of only the smaller one. Run the estimator once for each box, with that box's own dimensions, then combine the actual quote totals for your comparison.
Retaining measurements that remain useful

Attach a short contents description to each measurement set. For example, record that the photograph shows the parcel containing the jacket and both accessory cases after corner protection was added. If an item is removed the following day, create another record rather than overwriting the first. When the final statement differs from the initial estimate, you can then identify whether the difference belongs to a changed route, a changed parcel or a changed pricing input.

A good final check takes less time than investigating a mistaken quote. Read the three dimensions and their unit aloud, read the weight and its unit, confirm the destination, then confirm that every measurement describes the same physical box. Only at that point is the estimator result useful for comparing an offered service. If one measurement is still missing, state that explicitly when you share the result and keep the next decision conditional on obtaining it.
When the box has already left the warehouse

Once the parcel has been dispatched, use the dimensions listed on the actual parcel record for reconciliation. A later measurement taken after the box has been opened or flattened describes a different condition. If you question a recorded dimension, save the label and photographs of the unopened parcel before changing its shape.

articles.title: One HubBuy parcel or two? A like-for-like consolidation comparison
articles.lead: A combined shipment is worth comparing when it remains eligible for a suitable route and protects every item. Price the entire alternative, including every box, before acting on a single attractive quote.
sections: Start with the same list on both sides

Write the warehouse identifiers and quantities for all items under consideration. Copy that list before building your two scenarios. In the combined option, assign all selected items to one box. In the split option, assign each item to exactly one of two boxes. Check the totals: a missing accessory can make a split option appear artificially cheap, while a duplicated garment makes it seem expensive.
Establish why splitting might help

Perhaps only one item needs a rigid box, one piece must go to a different address, or a category affects route eligibility. Those are practical differences worth recording. If the two boxes go to different countries, you are evaluating a different delivery plan, not simply a cheaper arrangement for the same destination. Keep any urgency or special handling requirement visible alongside money.
Compare the full international cost

Suppose the combined option in a worked example is quoted at 164 units. The split option has one box quoted at 105 and a second at 72. The split total is 177 before any separately listed packing services. Looking only at the 105 would reverse the result. Add optional charges that apply twice and remove any charge shown as already included. Record the currency and timestamp for all quotations.
Check whether the estimates remain eligible

Use each box's own actual or proposed outer dimensions, weight and product category. If the combined package exceeds a route limit, strike out that route for that scenario. Never substitute the lighter box's weight for the combined box simply to obtain a result. Compare realistic packing arrangements and check that the selected service accepts all contents, including components that might be easy to forget in an accessory pocket.
Make a decision you can audit

Write the reason for the choice in ordinary language. It might be that the cheaper combined service satisfies all requirements, or that paying more for two boxes lets the urgent item leave before a later intake. Save the estimated difference separately from the eventual outcome. Once both parcels have been billed, compare each final entry against the estimate for the correct arrangement and explain any changed input.
An example where the larger box wins

Consider a fictional comparison for a buyer sending two hoodies and one rigid accessory case to the same address. The buyer wants the case protected and both hoodies included. Assume the offered combined arrangement costs 185 inclusive of the necessary protection. One separate parcel for the hoodies costs 102 and a second protected parcel for the case costs 96. Their sum is 198. On these particular assumptions the single-box option costs 13 less and satisfies the stated requirements.

Now add a condition: the quoted combined arrangement relies on removing the retail case, which the buyer needs as part of a gift. The 185 quote no longer describes an acceptable solution. Obtain a comparable combined quote that keeps the case, or mark that arrangement as unsuitable. The earlier numerical comparison still teaches something about what created the saving, but it cannot justify selecting a packing method that defeats the purpose of the purchase.
An example where smaller boxes remain worth considering

Take another fictional quote with a combined option at 214. The smaller boxes cost 112 and 94, for a total of 206, and their protective needs are already included. This time the arithmetic favours splitting by eight. Before deciding, verify whether there are additional services charged separately per parcel or any destination-specific conditions that were absent from the recorded totals. Two boxes can produce two delivery events and two references to monitor.

Suppose each smaller box also needs an explicitly quoted service costing five, while the combined option already includes it. The separate total becomes 216, two more than the combined quote. Such a narrow difference may be less important than arrival timing or how easily a recipient can receive two packages. Record the non-price reason for any choice so that a later invoice comparison is not mistaken for proof that the earlier decision was irrational.
How placement changes the measurement

A rectangular case can set the minimum width of a combined parcel. Soft clothing may fill empty space around it, or may require an increase in height once protection is included. Do not calculate a combined box by adding the item lengths, adding widths and adding heights independently. That describes a much larger imagined arrangement in most cases. Sketch how the pieces could sit and ask for relevant packed measurements or a realistic packing estimate.

The estimated split arrangement deserves the same care. A padded case may fit into one small carton, while the garments can use another shape. Give each box its intended packing and dimensions. Using a generous measured combined box alongside separate dimensions guessed from bare product photographs biases the result against consolidation. State the quality of your evidence for both scenarios. If a decision turns on a small difference, obtaining equivalent measurements can matter more than refining the arithmetic.
Organizing decisions around timing

A buyer might have one item already checked and another still waiting for a seller response. The combined quote assumes both will become eligible for shipment together. Record what you know about the later item and the storage status of the earlier one. A decision to split can address timing even if the combined quote has a small price advantage. State the timing requirement separately, for example that one item must leave before another has been inspected.

Avoid promising a delivery date on the basis of the number of boxes alone. A route estimate, seller delay, warehouse intake and final delivery can each describe a different stage. If the two pieces are needed as one matching set, splitting also creates a practical risk that one arrives earlier than its partner. If the pieces serve different recipients, the timing difference might be entirely acceptable. The right comparison includes how the items will actually be used.
Verify the plan after the warehouse acts

Once a packing decision has been confirmed, compare the assigned item list with the original scenario. Check that any separate accessory travelled with its intended parent item. In a split shipment, label the two parcel records clearly enough that the first delivery does not accidentally close the second. Keep the tracking number and payment for each box together. A notification about a single parcel can otherwise be mistaken for completion of the entire purchase.

When the actual charges arrive, compare them with the quote for the same configuration. If the courier or route differs, document that change before calculating a saving or overrun. Add the final charges for all boxes in the split option before stating its cost. The result becomes a useful comparison for this shipment. Retain the measured details with it rather than generalizing that consolidation, or splitting, will always be cheaper for a future order.
A second address changes the question

If one box will go directly to another person, include the cost and feasibility of forwarding an item locally under the combined arrangement. Compare delivery to both intended recipients, not simply delivery to the first address. Record which additional domestic leg is confirmed and which is hypothetical before making a claim about total savings.

articles.title: What does a HubBuy shipping estimate actually cover?
articles.lead: Read a freight result as a quotation for a named parcel, route and destination. Use it to answer the transport question it was calculated for, then check the remaining parts of your purchase separately.
sections: Read the inputs before the result

The HubBuy estimator accepts a destination and weight in grams and provides fields for product category and centimetre dimensions. An estimate based on a preset hoodie and one based on a measured packed box describe different evidence. Record which you used. A result without its inputs is difficult to reuse because you may later forget whether it covered a single garment or the full shipment.
Build an inclusion list

Put the route's displayed freight figure on one line. Beneath it, list each other cost you expect to encounter: seller price, domestic delivery, packing services and any other item actually named on the offer. Mark each one as included, separately quoted, already paid or unknown. Treat an omitted entry as unknown unless the live terms tell you otherwise. An estimate showing only international delivery cannot settle the price of seller-side goods.
Compare timing on the same basis

A delivery estimate may refer to a stage starting at dispatch. Read the route description before promising someone a date based on it. Include unresolved purchasing, seller dispatch, warehouse intake or packing in a separate planning timeline. Avoid adding arbitrary days to manufacture a confident arrival date. If the use date matters, state which pending event creates uncertainty and check the latest confirmed status.
Recheck destination details privately

The destination is part of the quote. Use the correct country and any region or postal information the estimator requests on the official page. If you share a comparison with someone, retain enough information to identify the route while removing the full delivery address. A screenshot of two prices cannot establish identical coverage when the destination fields are out of view.
When an item changes after quotation

Changing the contents, packing, measurements or selected services calls for a fresh estimate. Keep the old result because it can help explain a later difference. Mark the revised input with the reason for the change, such as a retained shoebox or a removed accessory. Ask HubBuy support about a specific line if the conditions appear identical but the quoted result still differs.
Mark the boundary of the estimate with an example

Imagine a buyer who has a confirmed merchandise total of 280 yuan, a domestic delivery charge of 12 and a screen showing an illustrative international freight estimate of 135. The cost recorded so far is 427, provided the freight estimate holds and there are no other separately applied charges. The 135 is not the price of the entire purchase. Equally, adding the 280 and 12 again to a consolidated budget that already includes those entries would overstate the amount.

Suppose the buyer keeps a separate running budget containing 292 already paid. To evaluate cash still needed, start with the prospective 135 and any other unpaid components that can be documented. To evaluate the total cost of acquiring and receiving the goods, include paid and unpaid components. Both calculations are valid, but they answer different questions. Label the output remaining payment or total purchase budget rather than presenting a single unexplained figure.
Compare two routes on one parcel

A route summary can show an estimated duration, price and brief notes, while a detail page may describe eligibility and service conditions. For a fair comparison, run both routes against the same parcel. Keep the destination, category, weight, outer dimensions, packing and declared contents consistent. Check what the figures include and whether one service shown in the summary becomes a separate charge later. If a route does not accept the contents, remove it from the usable comparison.

In a teaching exercise, route A displays 150 and route B displays 166. If A requires a separately quoted 12-unit service that B includes, the comparable amounts are 162 and 166. If B includes something you do not need and A needs nothing additional, the original 150 and 166 may be the relevant comparison. The example does not represent a real HubBuy route or a real price. Its purpose is to show why a service description can change which arithmetic belongs beside the price.
Translate uncertain components into clear questions

Use a short list with four statuses: included, already paid separately, confirmed additional cost, and unknown. Place each disputed component into one category only. For example, if an invoice confirms payment of domestic delivery with the seller order, do not also treat it as an unknown outbound fee. If the estimator does not explain how a particular optional service is handled, record the uncertainty beside that service.

Turn one unknown into one support question. Instead of asking whether the whole estimate is correct, specify that you entered a named destination and measured parcel, received a quote for a particular route, and need to know whether the selected packing service is already inside the displayed total. Save the answer with the date and the quote version. Avoid applying a reply about one route to a different service with different terms.
Use actual parcel changes to explain an apparent price change

The buyer may initially quote a single pair of shoes using a quick-estimate preset. Later the seller's box is retained, then a belt is added before international submission. The resulting packed measurements no longer describe the same shipment as the preset. Compare the revised quote with the final parcel statement, while keeping the original as evidence of how the budget developed. A difference between the first and last amounts is not automatically a new fee.

If you want to learn which change drove the difference, vary one input at a time in your own planning worksheet, provided the estimator supports the comparison. Keep the original destination and category, replace the assumed weight with the packed weight and record the result. Then apply the new dimensions. Label intermediate results as analytical scenarios rather than quotes for parcels you intend to send. If package category or eligibility changed, that can invalidate a direct one-input comparison.
Hand the result to another buyer clearly

A useful quote summary fits into a short paragraph: name the destination, contents, dimensions, scale weight, route, currency and the date of the estimate. Add a sentence identifying any fee that is known to be separate and any part still unresolved. Keep private delivery and payment details out of shared screenshots. Another buyer can then reproduce the estimate for the same inputs or identify why their own parcel differs.

When the parcel is ready, revisit the paragraph. Replace assumed measurements with confirmed ones, check that the route still appears and compare the actual payment request with the latest estimate. If an input is still provisional, say so before approving the expense. Keep the final payment record for reconciliation. The value of an estimate is its ability to support a decision under specified conditions, not its ability to guarantee a number after those conditions have changed.
Record who provided each figure

Put the source beside each amount when the seller, warehouse, and carrier all appear in one comparison. A seller’s approximate packed weight can be enough for an early screening decision. Once a warehouse measurement arrives, retain the seller figure in a separate column so a reader can see why the estimate changed and which measurement supported the eventual booking.

articles.title: How to reconcile a HubBuy parcel statement with your first quote
articles.lead: A good reconciliation tells you where a difference first appeared. Work in the original currency and parcel reference before looking at exchange effects or assuming a fee was added.
sections: Reconstruct the original comparison

Gather the original estimate, the warehouse submission and the final payment record. Confirm they refer to the same parcel contents and destination. A quote for two garments and a bill for two garments plus a box of shoes cannot be explained by checking the arithmetic alone. Keep the old list visible and make a separate column for the list eventually sent.
Compare physical inputs before money

Write the initial and final weight beside the initial and final outer dimensions. Record which inputs came from product presets, seller figures, proposed packing or an actual completed parcel. Put the route and service choice on the same row. If the original option disappeared because of a size limit, compare the final route's charge with a revised quote for that route rather than blaming every difference on the weight change.
Separate displayed totals from independent charges

Imagine that an estimated 140 rises to a final debit of 168. A final statement shows base freight of 156 and packing of 12. The first 16 of the difference comes from the freight line, and the remaining 12 is the packing line. The reconstructed final amount is 168. Do not sum 168, 156 and 12: the total already contains the two components.
Reconcile the payment destination

A coupon, account credit or refund can change the amount paid from an external card without changing the invoice subtotal. Record invoice total, balance used, external payment and credits as separate fields. When converting to your home currency, keep the original values intact and state the rate or posted amount used. If a promised credit has not posted, label it as pending instead of deducting it from the confirmed payment history.
Ask one question with the relevant evidence

If a difference remains, identify the charge and both records where you expected it to match. For example, ask which input changed the base freight between a named quote and a named parcel. Include the route, measurement date and currency, and omit unrelated payment details. HubBuy's public support page lists parcel submission, orders and shipping among its support topics. Use that channel for an explanation specific to your account.
A complete fictional reconciliation

Suppose the planning sheet contains an old seller subtotal of 220, domestic delivery of 10 and an outbound estimate of 145. The initial overall figure is 375. During packing the buyer adds a separately purchased accessory. Its purchase and domestic movement have already been recorded elsewhere. The outbound box also changes: the final freight line is 153 and the packing service line is 9. The new outbound total is 162. Comparing 162 with 145 gives a 17-unit change on the parcel side.

That 17 consists of eight more in the freight line and nine in the selected service under these example assumptions. It does not measure the cost of the accessory itself and should not be compared with the earlier all-purchase total of 375. Add the accessory's actual purchase entries separately if the question is total cost for the entire basket. Keep the same currency and identify whether any discount applies to freight, merchandise or the charge as a whole. The purpose is to reach an explanation for every difference without counting anything twice.
Distinguish invoice totals from sources of payment

Imagine the final parcel invoice is 162, the buyer uses 20 of account credit and the external card supplies the remaining 142. Checking only the card account might make the shipment look cheaper than it was. The invoice total still describes 162 of parcel charges. The payment history shows how that amount was settled. Record both pieces of information instead of replacing the invoice total with the smaller card debit.

The distinction also matters after a refund. Suppose six units are returned to the account balance later. Preserve the original 162 invoice, the original combination of payments and the separate six-unit credit with its destination. You can calculate a net cost when the refund is confirmed. If it has merely been requested, keep it in a pending column. That way one person reviewing the sheet for available funds and another reviewing it for net cost can both understand the figures.
Account for a route change before comparing rates

If the originally chosen route could not take the final parcel, compare the final statement with an estimate for the route that was actually used. Keep the old option separately and note why it became unavailable if the platform supplies a reason. A rate difference between two routes does not prove an unexpected change in the price of either route. Likewise, a change of destination or declared category can produce a different service set before weight and volume are even considered.

When the final route appears identical by name, check any displayed service variation or delivery zone. Two similar names may describe different delivery products. Compare actual route identifiers if the account exposes them. Save relevant screenshots with private addresses and payment information cropped out before sharing. If a code has changed but its meaning is unclear, ask support to confirm whether the quote and statement refer to the same service.
Reconcile several outbound packages against one original quote

A single initial estimate might turn into two shipments after an item is delayed. Compare their combined final cost with the original estimate only after identifying what changed. For example, two final parcels costing 88 and 76 have a combined cost of 164. Comparing only the 88 with the original estimate would leave the second box out; comparing each final box independently with the entire original estimate would count the same baseline twice.

Build a one-line contents list for each final parcel and match each original item exactly once. Identify excluded, returned or later-added items. If the contents have changed substantially, also retain a separate estimate calculated for the revised two-box arrangement. This new comparison is often better for checking the final charge, while the original estimate remains useful for understanding why the shopping plan exceeded the initial budget.
Decide whether the remaining difference is actionable

A small difference can come from rounding after currency conversion. It can also identify a real missing service line. Reconstruct the original-currency amounts first. Check whether rounding at the invoice level instead of at the item level accounts for the difference. If both the currency and all inputs match and a residual remains, do not create an unnamed miscellaneous charge just to make the sheet total agree. Preserve the residual and ask about it.

Send a message containing the parcel reference, original quote date, input measurements, final amount and arithmetic that remains unexplained. If the answer identifies an existing line, correct its classification instead of adding a duplicate. If a new credit is promised, follow it through to the account record. Close the reconciliation when both the invoice composition and the actual payment movements can be traced. Keep the dated comparison with the parcel documents for the next time you budget a similar shipment.
Keep a readable closing note

Write a one-sentence conclusion next to each resolved difference. For example, a previously unexplained charge might match a packing service on an earlier confirmation. Record that confirmation date and amount. Someone checking your records later can follow that connection even if the original transaction description was abbreviated.
